_doc: Key Themes registry (Macro › Key Themes; Jamie 10-28). One home for themes, signposts, scenarios and theme baskets. Claude maintains it in every market-thesis session (.agents/skills/fildi-market-thesis § Themes). Signpost kinds: chart (macro-charts cache series), fred (macro-data series field), revision (median LSEG 30-day EPS drift of a basket, %), flow (basket market-cap change minus whole-universe change, pp), cds (LSEG 5y CDS bp: level or change), gov (Treasury cash flows), manual (value typed here with as_of; stale after stale_days). bull_if / bear_if = [op, value]; neither → neutral. share_overrides = company-wide share count for dual-class names priced on one line (GOOGL = A+B+C, BRK.B in B-equivalents; approximate, re-check yearly). Thresholds are judgment calls labelled as such, not fitted — grading lives in theme_snapshots + LOG.md.

themes.thesis: Hyperscaler capex (~$700–800 B in 2026, > $1 T consensus 2027) keeps flowing to suppliers: chips, memory, optics, power.

view.text: Demand is real; money lands on suppliers, not spenders (A293).

themes.name: Inflation & the Fed
themes.thesis: Fed hiked in Sept (first since 2023). 1997 vs 2000/2018 split = whether the Fed keeps hiking.

view.text: One-and-done is the A-path; a Dec hike moves weight to B.

themes.name: Geopolitical tension & oil
themes.thesis: Conflict risk (Middle East / Iran, Russia–Ukraine, US–China trade and chips) reaches markets through oil → inflation → the Fed, and through supply chains (rare earths, chips).

view.text: GPR ~94th percentile since 2000 and WTI ~$108: oil is the channel that can turn scenario A into B (an Iran deal is the D-path trigger).

refs: Caldara & Iacoviello (2022) AER: high GPR → lower investment, higher disaster risk

themes.name: Crowd sentiment (contrarian)
themes.thesis: Crowd fear and greed run to extremes before turns: extreme fear = premium is rich and forced sellers leave cheap longs; extreme greed = premium is thin and run-ups are crowded. Read it contrarian.

view.text: Fear & Greed 35 and 5-day put/call 0.96 (median): fear side of neutral, no extreme yet. At an extreme, look for opportunity (fear) or get careful (greed); the market-state engine decides the timing.

playbook.do: Panic sets up the best put weeks: wait for VIX ÷ VIX3M < 1 (selloff done), then sell closer — that turn is where sharp-drop weeks earn +45→+101 bp/wk. Until then new puts lose at every band, so hold cash and build the list.
playbook.evidence: S101: panic loses at every band 2019–22 (−35..−74 bp/wk)

playbook.do: After a V-shaped drop with the vol curve back in contango, sell puts closer (higher Δ): net bp rises steeply with Δ.
Rally: premium barely rises with Δ but tail loss rises 4–40× → far strikes keep the pay with a fraction of the risk. Upside belongs to shares held, not short calls into run-ups.
playbook.evidence: S101 (rally flat in bp, tail ×4–40); S087 (short calls lose −30..−36 bp/wk when a run-up is forecast)

playbook.do: Slow bear: market-wide edge is thin (≤ +7 bp/wk 2019–22), so keep the engine band and a smaller book; where it still pays: put-edge Q1–3 names inside sector drops (+51…+89 bp/wk, S102).
playbook.evidence: S101 bear grind ≤ +7 bp/wk 2019–22; S102 put-edge inside sector_drop

playbook.do: Edge lives in cash-secured puts (best return per risk) and jade lizards. Spreads, condors, iron flies, calendars, debit spreads and long straddles lost as single trades 2021→; combos and the long side are being re-tested (A297) before any use.
playbook.evidence: S076 (781k trades 2021→): CSP +0.51 %/trade t 5.1; jade lizard t 6.5; calendar −7 % t −4.1

playbook.do: Index options price ~2× the drop risk that shows up → selling index put premium is paid; buying index protection is expensive insurance.
playbook.evidence: S057: model vs VIX barrier odds +0.205 skill (holdout 29 % implied vs 14 % realized)

playbook.do: Use macro, themes and the cycle label to pick where to look (sectors, baskets, which names to research) and to explain; time collateral, band and size off the tested market state instead — macro timing failed every test.
playbook.evidence: S006, S027 (0/12 regimes pass), S057 direction = base rate, S087 (drawdowns unforecastable)

playbook.do: Extreme fear (F&G < 25): look for opportunity — index put premium is richest (S057), and once the vol curve is back in contango the engine sells closer (S101 sharp drop). Build the long list from names whose revisions hold up.
playbook.evidence: S057, S101 (states tested; the F&G cut itself untested on our puts — S102/S107 per-stock F&G added nothing)

playbook.do: Extreme greed (F&G > 75): premium is thin and run-ups crowded → keep puts far, no adding size, no short calls into the run; trim winners rather than chase.
playbook.evidence: S101 rally (flat bp, tail ×4–40), S087/S106 (short calls lose into run-ups); F&G cut untested

playbook.do: Revisions turning down: misses move ~3× beats, so short puts through earnings carry the bigger side of the asymmetry → use the engine's far-strike earnings rule.
playbook.evidence: S120 (asymmetry real, every year); revision-regime × structure test pending (earnings-cycle study)

playbook.do: High-yield spread > 4 %: stress spreads to levered names → their puts pay more, so take them only far and small; cash-funded megacaps are where closer strikes still fit.
playbook.evidence: Thesis claim 10 (telecom 2000 analog); not backtested on our puts

playbook.do: Oil > $100: inflation risk keeps the Fed hiking (scenario B) → keep the band on Auto, watch energy-sensitive names (airlines, cruise, chemicals) for far strikes only.
playbook.evidence: Untested; geopolitics × structure test pending (GPR study)

playbook.do: Long convexity after crashes is where fear pays if structured right: big intraday reversals cluster in high-fear days (Mar 2020, Apr 2025). Plain long 0DTE averages −53 % for retail (spreads, capped tests) — S124–S126 iterate strike, timing, short side and combos to find the version that works.
playbook.evidence: S048, S053; Beckmeyer–Branger–Gayda 2023 (SSRN 4404704); base rates 10-28: ≥ 3 % intraday drops 3.6/yr, reversal calls ITM 17 %, mostly 2020
